source.title: Optima: Optimizing Effectiveness and Efficiency for LLM-Based Multi-Agent System
source.authors: Weize Chen; Jiarui Yuan; Chen Qian; Cheng Yang; Zhiyuan Liu; Maosong Sun

record.tranche_reason: The study measures downstream task performance as inference-time sampling compute increases, using self-consistency steps rather than training-scale sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper reports inference-time self-consistency scaling curves and statements about coverage and majority-voting accuracy. It does not test held-out pretraining loss against parameter count, training tokens, or training compute; nor small-run extrapolation, compute-optimal training allocation, architecture sensitivity, other modalities or training regimes, or fitting dependence. Training-scaling-law references are background, not results from this study.
record.test_reason: The study varies inference-time sampling at fixed model size and evaluates OPTIMA's task performance and token efficiency. It does not test downstream predictability from model/training scale or pretraining loss (V6), nor any other listed version. Inference-time scaling is a related claim requiring its own version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the inference-scaling findings. The authors' broader conclusion is that OPTIMA training improves multi-agent communication efficiency and task performance, transfers within related domains, and enables more effective inference-time sampling. They report logarithmic coverage gains, earlier majority-voting plateaus, and the stated 88.5% token saving; they do not establish training-scale power laws.
record.recipe_differences: Measures self-consistency inference sampling and task performance, rather than training-run loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or training compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome differs by metric: coverage scales log-linearly, whereas majority-voting accuracy tends to plateau; the paper also notes weaker majority-voting improvement on information-exchange tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.3 and Appendix A report approximately log-linear gains in coverage with increasing self-consistency samples across OPTIMA variants and tasks. Debate coverage is any-correct coverage; IE coverage is average best F1 among samples.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: At fixed model size, increasing inference-time sampling improves oracle best-of-samples task performance approximately linearly in log sample count over the tested range.

fits_no_version.finding: Majority-voting performance tends to plateau earlier than coverage; IE voting gains are less pronounced and may depend on the F1-based grouping procedure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Realized gains from additional inference samples depend on answer selection and task, with majority voting saturating before oracle coverage.

fits_no_version.finding: GSM8k-trained OPTIMA-iDPO matches CoT-SC performance with 88.5% fewer inference tokens in Section 3.3.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training for communication efficiency can improve the downstream performance-versus-inference-token frontier.

record.problems: The scaling curves are presented as figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study evaluates inference-time sampling rather than the training-scaling quantities in the main claim.
record.rows_left_out: No reported self-consistency scaling curves left out. Benchmark comparisons in Table 1 are not rows because they do not vary scale; cited results from other studies are excluded.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or training compute over several orders of magnitude.
Prediction of much larger training-run losses from small-run power-law fits.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocation and stable allocation exponents.
Architecture effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law loss relationships in other modalities or training regimes; fine-tuning and transfer comparisons alone do not test the form.
Predictable downstream improvement with model/training scale or pretraining loss. Sampling more answers from fixed models tests a separate inference-time relationship.
Dependence of fitted training-scaling exponents and compute-optimal allocation on setup or fitting choices, including departures from single power laws.

record.verdict_notes: All corrected states describe the rows' inability to determine a listed version, not absence of the reported inference-time effects. The supplied text extraction does not preserve plotted curves sufficiently to verify individual figure-only values or assign each voting curve a separate effect state. The 3B/8B results assess robustness across different base models, and the two-/three-agent comparisons change task configuration; neither establishes downstream scaling predictability.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens, or training compute.
Prediction of larger training-run losses from smaller-run fits.
Architecture-shape effects at fixed parameter count.
Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.
The study varies inference-time self-consistency sampling, not model size or pretraining loss; it does not test whether pretraining loss predicts downstream performance.
Dependence of training-scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocation on fitting and setup choices.
